steps.say: Editing improves meaning and style. Proofreading corrects mistakes.
Check that verbs agree with their subjects and that tenses stay consistent.
steps.show: Each of the pupils has a locker.

steps.say: Watch out for commonly confused words.
steps.show: its or it’s     fewer or less     their, there or they’re

steps.say: Make sure every sentence is complete and every opening phrase clearly describes its subject.
Replace repeated or vague words with precise details.

options.text: There are fewer cars on the road today.
There are less cars on the road today.
options.why: Cars can be counted, so use fewer.

options.text: There is fewer cars on the road today.
options.why: Cars is plural, so use are.

options.text: There are fewest cars on the road today.
options.why: Fewest is used to compare three or more things.

hints: Cars are things you can count.
Use fewer with things you can count.
Check the verb too: is or are?
check.explanation: Cars can be counted, so we use fewer, and cars is plural, so we use are.

check.prompt: One word is spelt wrongly. Write it correctly. The hotel had excellent accomodation.
hints: This word has two sets of double letters.
Think of it as having room for two c letters and two m letters.
Write acco, then think about the next double letter.
check.explanation: Accommodation has a double c and a double m: ac-com-mo-da-tion.
